findings.breaking_input: A Cloudflare reply of HTTP 200 with `{"success":true,"result":{}}` to GET /zones, or `"result":[null]`, or a dns_records GET with `"result":null`. A DoH answer of `{"Answer":"x"}` or `{"Answer":[null]}` for verify.
findings.why: The `errors || []` fix covered only the error path. `(found || []).find` throws on a non-array object, and `bare(r.name)` throws on a null element, so the adapter dies with a raw TypeError. `(records || []).filter` and `r.comment` fail the same way. `result: null` on a records GET is treated as 'no records exist', which skips the FOREIGN_RECORD refusal and goes straight to POST. `cnames` calls `.filter` on a non-array `Answer`. `r.google` is dereferenced without checking that `probe.doh` returned an object.
findings.fix: Add one helper that returns an array of plain objects or throws a fixed-message error. Use it on every `result`, `Answer` and `doh` reply. Treat `result: null` on a records GET as a refusal, not an empty list.
findings.twin_of: `errors || []` trusted the provider to send an array of objects -> every `x || []` over a response body

findings.breaking_input: Slot timeout fires while `zoneOf` or the records GET is in flight. `cf()` passes no `signal` to `ctx.fetch`, and `scaffold` never checks `ctx.signal.aborted` before the POST or PATCH.
findings.why: If ctx.fetch does not bind the signal itself, a stalled request outlives the slot timeout. When it finally answers, scaffold goes on to create the CNAME after the runner has already recorded failed(timeout). That breaks the REQ-02(c) promise that the AbortSignal stops further creates. The `zoneOf` loop makes up to N sequential GETs with no abort check either. The contract test only exercises the abort path in `verify`.
findings.fix: Pass `signal: ctx.signal` in `cf()` and throw ABORTED before every mutating call and every `zoneOf` iteration. Add a scaffold arm that aborts between the GET and the POST and asserts zero POSTs.
findings.twin_of: A sleep listened for "abort" on a signal that had already fired, so the slot timeout was swallowed for the whole poll -> every wait, retry or poll loop in an adapter or the runner

findings.breaking_input: A resolver or provider string carrying U+00AD (soft hyphen), U+034F, U+180E, U+3164 or U+115F (invisible fillers), tag characters U+E0020-U+E007F, U+FFF9-U+FFFB (interlinear annotation), or an unpaired surrogate such as `\ud800`.
findings.why: SKIP was widened for U+061C and the zero-width marks, but the same invisible and format-character classes are still printed. Tag characters can carry hidden text into the board. Lone surrogates survive the code-point iteration and print as replacement characters. Each round has added only the characters its attacker listed, not the Unicode category.
findings.fix: Drop every `\p{Cf}`, `\p{Cc}`, `\p{Zl}`, `\p{Zp}`, `\p{Cs}` and `\p{Co}` character, plus U+3164, U+115F and U+034F. Test one sample per category.
findings.twin_of: The sanitiser missed U+061C and the zero-width marks, and capped by UTF-16 units -> every sanitiser and every `.slice(0, n)` on display text

findings.breaking_input: An error object without `code`, a DoH answer with `data: null`, or a record with no `type` or `id`.
findings.why: `say(v)` runs `String(v)`, so undefined or null becomes the text 'undefined' or 'null'. That is the same coercion defect fixed for `ctx.upstream`. The reason reads `undefined: msg`, FOREIGN_RECORD names `undefined undefined`, and a null CNAME `data` becomes the label 'null' that `cnames` compares and prints.
findings.fix: Return '' from `say` for a non-string, non-number input. Omit empty fields from messages.
findings.twin_of: Upstream entries were coerced with `String()`, so a `null` id became the hostname "null" -> every value one adapter hands another through state

findings.breaking_input: A catalog row with a bare `depends_on:` or `optional_for:` key and no value, which the subset parser reads as null. Also a non-string entry in `depends_on` that other lint rules read before this check runs.
findings.why: `s[k] !== undefined` makes a valueless key fail as 'must be a list' even though it is the natural empty form. The DAG, edge and predicate rules may already call `.has`, `.map` or `new Set` on the entries before this check reaches them. The new lines are placed after rules that read the same fields, so a non-string entry can crash the lint with a TypeError instead of producing the list-shape finding. The 123 mutant passes only because the DAG rules happen to tolerate numbers.
findings.fix: Run the list-shape check first and skip the rules that read the field once it fails. Decide explicitly whether null is allowed for an empty list.
findings.twin_of: A quoted YAML list item holding `: ` was parsed as a one-key mapping -> every YAML field the code reads as a string: assert its type, not its presence

findings.breaking_input: A hosting slot that is `verified` but whose `resources` hold two `dns-target` entries after a re-scaffold, with the old target kept alongside the new one. Then `apply dns`.
findings.why: State resources accumulate across attempts and nothing here dedupes them. dns then refuses with 'hosting reported 2 dns-target resources', which blames the wrong slot. The runner has no re-entry path to retire a stale upstream value. Separately, nothing in the diff shows that `slotRow` returns an object for a dependency with no state row; if it returns undefined, `r.state` throws before the worker writes a receipt.
findings.fix: Have the runner replace a slot's resources by kind on re-scaffold. Make the worker use `(slotRow(st0, d) || {})`. Add a runner test for a dependency with no state row.
findings.twin_of: upstream handed an adapter resources from a dependency that had failed after recording them -> every value passed between slots: is its producer's state checked?
